situation: One licensed, unedited camera-followed park take in which two people progress from hand contact through separation, reconvergence, lift, shared movement and a native frame exit.
hypotheses_under_test: A readable hand-contact anchor can establish the relationship before density rises.
Progressively adding live distance, reconvergence and lift states inside one frame can compress relationship development without becoming three decorative duplicates.
A 9.48-second native lift, carry, run, full frame-exit and measured empty-path release can restore breath after the dense state without freeze, retime, zoom or generated imagery.
The lower-right lift window can hand its next native source frame directly to the full canvas, making the screen-within-screen state a transition anchor rather than decoration.
Replacing simultaneous support windows with one sequential support role at a time can preserve the density wave while reducing competition with the central pair.
The same density-wave-release Operator should remain legible in a two-person playful relationship situation independent from flower-field and interior-light material.
purpose: Test density-wave-release in a two-person relationship-action situation using one coherent source take and a long native movement release.

strengths: one continuous take with stable pair identity, wardrobe, park axis and overcast light
distinct relationship states change distance, touch, action ownership and shared direction
the lift and run provide a genuine physical climax
both performers leave the frame and the path continues moving natively
limits: the camera follows the pair, so a vertical cover crop would remove relationship information
the playful action does not test conflict, reconciliation, hierarchy or product advertising
the panel state must remain brief so the two-person action is not reduced to a collage
